Lift the difference eigenvector to w and remove its bath mean. B(Lw-lambda w)=0 makes the residual constant; its zero bath expectation makes it zero. Nonnegative nonzero differences make w monotone and nonconstant.

The pairwise covariance formula then gives strictly negative derivative of the Gibbs expectation at every finite positive beta, since at least one strictly ordered pair contributes positively. Bath mean zero gives normal absolute-overlap ordering on both sides.

derivative_geometry_and_finite_test: Adjoining the constant column makes W(pi1prime,...,pikprime)=W(1,pi1,...,pik). Multiplying every function by Z multiplies the determinant by Z^(k+1), via a triangular product-rule row transformation.

Expand W(Z,f1,...,fk) in its first column. Repeated-column terms vanish, and the remaining exponential Vandermonde determinants give the printed sign (-1)^(k(k-1)/2), prefix energy-gap product and positive tail sum. This indexed argument works for every k<n.
For n=4, g=pi1prime>0 at all finite real beta. The k=2 identity gives g^2 uprime<0. The k=3 identity gives g^3(uprime)^3 d2v/du2<0, so v as a function of u has strictly positive curvature.

The mixed two-column Wronskian ratio gives s(x)=(c2 x^gamma-c0)/(c0+c1 x). All c_i>0, gamma>1; the printed derivative numerator is positive. s rises strictly from -1 to s(1)>-1 as x goes from zero to one.

For bprime=g Phi with Phi=A+B u+C v, C=0 gives a monotone or constant Phi. For C nonzero, Phiprime=uprime(B+C s); it has precisely one positive-beta critical point if -B/C lies strictly between -1 and s(1), otherwise none. Equality at either boundary yields no interior critical point.

The listed endpoint values and optional critical value are therefore the exact infimum/supremum on each bath side. Opposite strict signs occur in the open interval if and only if the finite list has min<0<max; limiting strict signs persist at finite beta by continuity.

Strict convexity gives at most two derivative zeros counting multiplicity: a nonvertical line meets a strictly convex graph at most twice, tangency has exactly order two, and C=0 has at most one. Identically zero derivative would force constant w by independence of exponentials, excluded by nonzero bath-orthogonal w.

For opposite signs on cooling, the last sign-changing zero before the bath has nonzero b and creates increasing magnitude immediately to its left. For heating use the first sign-changing zero after the bath and decreasing magnitude immediately to its right.
Tangencies without opposite signs do not suffice. A stationary bath or an endpoint equality does not create an additional interior root. Finite positive witnesses follow from the open sign intervals.
